newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric says CE's offer too low.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric says CE's offer too low.

text.p: Northern Electric Plc said Monday that CalEnergy Co. Inc.'s $1.1 billion hostile takeover bid was too low, but the Omaha-based utility said it would press ahead with its offer.

In its first formal response to the Nov. 5 offer by CalEnergy's CE Electric unit, Northern Electric said the 630 pence ($10.51) bid was "below even the lowest price put to Northern Electric by the bidder prior to the launch of its hostile offer."

CE Electric, which has already bought nearly 30 percent of the British regional electricity company, said it still felt its offer was full and fair, adding that there was "nothing in Northern Electric's defence document which changes our view."
CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, denied Northern's assertion that CE had suggested a price of 700 pence ($11.68) a share.
"This ambitious range was entirely the proposal of Northern Electric's board," it said.
Northern said it would be announcing its latest financial results by the end of this month and would provide shareholders with "important financial information" demonstrating its value.
"Northern Electric is worth more to CE Electric," the company said in a statement.
